_note: Settled English copy decisions, read by tools/authoring/copy_standard.py.
This file is empty on purpose, and the emptiness is the point. The Korean
table exists because two proofreading rounds produced rules; the English
corpus has had a pilot review but has never had its accepted wording written
down anywhere a check could reach. Until then the mechanism runs green here
It is here rather than waiting to be created because of what happened the
last time a general rule was filed under one language: the contract was a
Korean document with an English appendix until 2026-08-22, and both curricula
spent a week re-deriving each other's rules a day apart. A rule that is true
of both languages belongs in shared/ux-philosophy.md; a wording decision that
is true only of English belongs here, in the same shape as the Korean one.
Rule kinds and fields: see the header of tools/authoring/copy_standard.py.
Note that kana sound anchors are a Korean-only device, so the Korean table's
`pair` rules have no English analogue — but `run` and `glossary` do, and the
slang-gloss rule in particular would transfer to English as written.
